claims.text: Hot soba is served in a dashi- and shoyu-based broth, and cold soba comes with a shoyu-based dipping sauce (tsuyu) — both traditional preparations that contain wheat via soy sauce.
Menu includes vegetable tempura, cold eggplant (nasu), and natto dishes alongside the standard soba, giving some plant-forward options on the menu (though broths are traditionally dashi-based).

name: 高級伊奈利寿司専門店 福寿家 (Fukujuya (Kokyu Inari-zushi Senmon-ten Fukuj)

claims.text: Every publicly described variety of the shop's inari sushi (classic broth-simmered, salt-seasoned, sweet potato, lotus root, pickled ginger) is built from tofu, rice, and vegetables, with no meat or seafood toppings mentioned in any source reviewed.

name: 元祖油堂 宮益坂店 (Ganso Aburado Miyamasuzaka)

claims.text: The chain's official allergy information chart lists wheat (小麦), egg, and dairy as allergens present in the oil-noodle dish, consistent with the soy-based tare and standard wheat noodle used chain-wide.
The chain publishes a printed allergen chart per menu item, noting that sensitivity varies by individual and the chart is meant as a reference rather than a guarantee against reactions.

name: GARB pintino（ガーブ ピンティーノ） (Garb Pintino)

claims.text: Guidance associated with the restaurant's booking listings states that customers with food allergies or ingredients they cannot eat should call the restaurant in advance so staff can confirm what can be accommodated.
Reports associated with the restaurant's listings note that when guests informed the restaurant of allergies or disliked ingredients ahead of time, the accommodation was handled attentively.

The kitchen sources organic vegetables and uses fresh, traceable contract-farm meat, and cooking relies mainly on charcoal grilling plus imported spices/herbs/citrus rather than heavy sauces, which may make it easier to identify and discuss individual allergens with staff.

name: ごちそう焼むすび おにまる 西新宿店 (Gochisou Yaki Musubi Onimaru Nishi-Shinjuku)

claims.text: Several signature onigiri, such as the tuna mayo and salmon rice balls, are finished with a traditional "kaeshi" simmered soy sauce, a style of Japanese soy sauce that typically contains wheat.

name: グリル グランド (Grill Grand)

claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free preparation area or fryer is indicated anywhere; the crab cream croquette (a breaded, deep-fried item) is one of the restaurant's signature dishes, implying a shared fryer used for wheat-breaded foods.

name: ハヌリ 渋谷本店 (Hanuri Shibuya Honten)

claims.text: Vegetable-forward sides — grilled kimchi, negi (scallion) salad, house miso and lettuce/perilla wrapping leaves for samgyeopsal — are described as free refills, giving vegetarian/vegan diners extra plant-based options to fill up on alongside the meat menu.
